method: I plan to make a short self-introduction animation using a cartoon version of myself. The character will wave, change expressions, and introduce my interests through small drawings and short texts. I want to add a soft pop when an object appears and a light sound when the character moves. I will first draw a storyboard, then make the frames and add sound. I will adjust the timing so that viewers have enough time to read each sentence.
related_work: The animation examples in the course gave me different ideas. In Fantasmagorie, simple lines change into new shapes. In Duck Amuck, changes to the image and sound affect how we understand the character. These examples made me consider what movement and sound could add to my own drawings.
results_discussion: The animation is still at the planning stage, so I cannot judge the final effect yet. However, I am starting to think about what the sound adds to the drawings. A small movement may feel more playful when it is matched with a short sound. Too many effects could also distract viewers from the introduction. I want the cute style to show my personality, while keeping the information easy to follow. I will need to test this balance during editing
title: week 6
introduction: This week, I learned how animation can show feelings through movement, sound, and timing. This connects to our project, May It Stay. I am planning a short celebration animation for the end of the game, so I started thinking about how a few simple drawings could make the moment feel warm.
